correctness.rationale: For odd q two-point Hermite interpolation determines one monic quartic for each ordered distinct repeated-root pair, yielding q(q-1) incidences. Any multiple counting occurs precisely through squares of split monic quadratics; these contribute q(R4(c)+R4(-c))/2 to subtract. Irreducible quadratic square cases add q(H(c)+H(-c)) through their unique rational critical point. The formula B=q(q-1)+q(H(c)+H(-c)-(R4(c)+R4(-c))/2) gives three cases for q congruent 1 mod 8 (fourth power, square not fourth, nonsquare) and q(q-1) for other odd q. For characteristic two, f'=aT^2+d; if a=d=0 exactly q^2 quartics are simultaneously nonsquarefree, otherwise the shifted polynomials cannot both have a repeated root. Inclusion-exclusion gives C=q^4-2q^3+B; covariance (B-q^2)/q^4. Independent polynomial-gcd enumeration confirmed all nonzero shifts for q=2,3,5,7; the bundled independent finite-field quotient checker and 12-field/88-shift claimed output were read, but not wholly rerun. General prime powers rely on analytic proof.
